newsitem.title: CHINA: China urged to set up forex lending market.
newsitem.headline: China urged to set up forex lending market.

text.p: An official Chinese newspaper on Wednesday called for quick action to set up a national market to allow local banks to lend and borrow foreign exchange funds among themselves.
Analysts said such a market would help Chinese banks save foreign currency, but said there was no sign yet that Beijing had begun to plan its establishment.
The Shanghai-based Business News said China's current foreign exchange market was imperfect without such an interbank foreign exchange lending market.

Chinese banks currently cannot make good use of their surplus foreign exchange or cover short-term shortages because foreign currency sums are allowed to circulate only within a bank, but not between different banks, it said.

Analysts said because of domestic restrictions, many Chinese banks and major firms put their surplus foreign exchange in banks outside China at relatively low interest rates and borrowed abroad at higher interest rates than necessary.
"Losses are considerable," said one Chinese banker. "Setting up an interbank lending market would help save a lot foreign exchange."
"There is little foreign currency liquidity among Chinese banks," said one Shanghai banker. "There is a huge waste of resources."
Officials at the People's Bank of China, the central bank, and the State Administration for Foreign Exchange Control, declined to comment.

Beijing launched a trial interbank lending market early this year to allow Chinese banks to lend and borrow renminbi on a short-term basis as a key step towards building market-driven financial markets in China.

China has a foreign exchange trading market, allowing banks to swap local currency for U.S. and Hong Kong dollars and Japanese yen. But there is no formal mechanism at present for banks to lend foreign exchange funds to each other.

"Foreign exchange lending business is an important part of a foreign exchange market," the Business News said. "To set up an interbank foreign exchange lending market would be an important step for China as part of its financial reforms.
"If China can establish an interbank lending market for foreign exchange, it would help make best use of its foreign exchange resources," the paper added.

Beijing has allowed branches of overseas banks in China to settle foreign exchange accounts for foreign-invested firms in China since July 1. The paper said this had made the setting up of such a foreign exchange market even more urgent.

At a seminar in Beijing in late August, Chinese bankers proposed the market be opened to designated banks and financial departments of major companies in its initial stages before being open to all major financial institutions.
The Business News proposed Shanghai as the venue for the market. It said the city had a good financial background and that Beijing aimed to build the city into an international financial centre.
